transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Mr. Hassan, thank you for coming back in to see me today. I wanted to speak with you personally because there is something I need to address regarding your last scan.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I'm already here. I assume this is about the one from three months ago. The other doctor told me everything was fine.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know that is what you were told, and that is exactly why I am here. I am so sorry, but we made a mistake. A finding on your imaging that required a follow-up scan was missed by our team and not communicated to you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Typical. Just typical. What do you mean missed? You can't just miss something on a scan.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I realize how frustrating and exhausting this is for you, especially given everything you've had to deal with in this clinic before. I take full responsibility for this. We failed to ensure that every part of the report was reviewed and acted upon.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So the other guy lied to me. Or he's just as careless as the rest of you. I'm sitting here with chronic pain and now I find out you people can't even read a report?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is completely understandable that you feel cynical about this. It feels like another failure in a long line of them. I can't imagine how tiring it is to keep encountering these hurdles when you are already dealing with so much pain.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't want to hear how you imagine it. I want to know what was actually on the scan.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There was a small area of concern—what we call an incidental finding—on the edge of the lung. It wasn't the primary reason for the scan, but it's something that needs a follow-up image to make sure it hasn't changed.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: An incidental finding. That's a fancy way of saying you found something and forgot to tell me.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: You're right. It is a failure of our process. I am deeply sorry that we let this happen and that you were given the wrong information.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So what now? Do I just wait another three months for someone else to forget?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: No, we are going to prioritize this immediately. I have already contacted the radiology department. I have a slot reserved for you this coming Thursday at 10:00 AM for a repeat scan to get an updated look at that area.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Thursday. I have to take time off work again.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know this is a huge imposition on your time and your energy. I will personally track the results of that scan the moment they are released. I will call you on your mobile by Friday at 4:00 PM, regardless of whether the results are in or if we are still waiting, just so you aren't left wondering.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And how do I know you won't just miss another sub-section of the report?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: That is a fair question. To prevent this from happening again, I have flagged your chart with a mandatory review alert. I've also spoken with the department head to change how these secondary findings are flagged so that the primary team cannot clear a patient without confirming that specific section has been read.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It sounds good. It always sounds good when you're apologizing.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know my words don't fix the fact that this happened, and I know trust is earned, not requested. I am committed to seeing this through personally.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Fine. Thursday at ten.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll make sure the registration desk has everything ready so you don't have to wait in the lobby. I will send you a confirmation text right now with the appointment details. Is there anything else, even a small detail, that's worrying you right now?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Just the fact that I have to keep coming back here.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I hear you. It's exhausting. I'll do everything I can to make sure the rest of this process is seamless for you.

H.justification: The resident never interrupts, remains regulated despite the patient's cynicism, and allows the patient to express frustration without rushing.

E.justification: The error was named explicitly and lay language was used, but the resident never performed a comprehension check (e.g., 'Does that make sense?').

A.justification: The resident used direct apology language, took full responsibility ('I take full responsibility for this'), and maintained accountability throughout the patient's pushback.

R.justification: The resident named specific emotions ('frustrating', 'exhausting', 'cynical') and referenced the patient's specific history of pain and previous clinic hurdles.

T.justification: The resident provided a specific date/time for the scan, a specific follow-up timeline (Friday at 4:00 PM), and detailed systemic prevention measures.
